title: NISM Investment Adviser (Series X-A and X-B)
blurb: Exam prep for the Investment Adviser certification: SEBI IA rules, fee-only advice, risk profiling, financial planning, tax, insurance, retirement and products.

rows: Aspiring SEBI-registered investment advisers and anyone giving personalised, fee-based advice
About 134 minutes of lessons, then cards, checkpoints and the final quiz
None. Module 19 (NISM V-A) helps with product basics
21 short lessons in 4 stages, each ending with three exam-style checks
outcomes: Explain who must register as an investment adviser and the fee-only rule.
Run client onboarding, risk profiling and suitability with proper records.
Build a goal-based plan using time value of money, insurance, tax and retirement logic.
Compare equity, debt, mutual fund, PMS, AIF and REIT options for a client.
Handle conflicts, segregation and disclosures correctly.

sources: SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 and later amendments and circulars (check the current text)
NISM-Series-X-A and X-B: Investment Adviser (Level 1 and Level 2) workbooks (current editions)
Income-tax Act provisions: rates and limits change, verify before advising
Practice exam only: confirm the current NISM exam format and eligibility before booking

final.title: NISM Investment Adviser (Series X-A and X-B) final quiz

questions.q: Personalised advice on securities for a fee requires registration as:
questions.why: Personalised advice for consideration falls under the IA regulations.

questions.q: Investment adviser advice is:
questions.why: The client decides and executes.

questions.q: Which fee modes are available to an IA?
questions.why: Fixed fee or a percentage of assets under advice, both within caps.

questions.q: An IA should keep records for at least:
questions.why: Five years is the minimum record retention.

questions.q: An investment adviser may collect fees in advance for at most:
questions.why: At most one quarter in advance.

questions.q: AUA fee of 1.5% on ₹40 lakh gives, per year:
An individual IA offering distribution to advisory clients is:
questions.why: Advice and distribution must be separate.

questions.q: When advising on mutual funds, an IA should prefer:
questions.why: Direct plans carry no distributor commission.

questions.q: Risk capacity is:
questions.why: Capacity is the ability to absorb losses.

questions.q: When capacity is lower than tolerance, advice should follow:
questions.why: Use the lower of the two.

questions.q: A common emergency fund target is:
questions.why: Three to six months of expenses.

questions.q: Income ₹1 lakh, EMIs ₹45,000. The debt-service ratio is:
₹1 lakh at 10% for 3 years becomes:
Real return when nominal is 10% and inflation 6% is about:
The most cost-efficient life cover for income replacement is:
questions.why: Term insurance is pure protection at the lowest cost.

questions.q: Human life value is based on:
questions.why: HLV discounts the income the family depends on.

questions.q: Under the old regime, deductions include:
questions.why: The old regime allows deductions such as 80C and 80D.

questions.q: Tax-saving investments should be chosen:
o: For the goal first, then tax
questions.why: Goal fit comes first.

questions.q: A 4% withdrawal rate on ₹8 lakh annual need gives a corpus of:
Sequence risk is:
o: Poor returns early in retirement withdrawals
questions.why: Early losses while withdrawing hurt more.

questions.q: The PPF term is:
questions.why: PPF has a 15-year term.

questions.q: SCSS is open to:
questions.why: Age 60 and above (with limited exceptions).

questions.q: A long-term target mix is:
questions.why: Strategic allocation is the long-term policy mix.

questions.q: Diversification mainly reduces:
questions.why: Specific risk can be diversified away.

questions.q: Overlap between funds means:
questions.why: Overlap is the same stocks held in several funds.

questions.q: A low tracking error is preferred for:
questions.why: Index products should follow their index closely.

questions.q: Price 300, EPS 15. P/E is:
Dividend ₹6 on price ₹300 gives a yield of:
When yields rise, bond prices:
questions.why: Prices move opposite to yields.

questions.q: A credit rating measures:
questions.why: Ratings assess the likelihood of default.

questions.q: The PMS minimum investment (per current rules) is:
questions.why: The PMS minimum is ₹50 lakh.

questions.q: A venture capital AIF belongs to:
questions.why: Venture capital funds are Category I.

questions.q: Using options to protect a portfolio is:
questions.why: Protection against loss is hedging.

questions.q: The best return measure for monthly SIP cash flows is:
questions.why: XIRR handles irregular dated cash flows.

questions.q: Selling in a panic after a fall is linked to:
questions.why: Loss aversion makes losses feel larger than gains.

questions.q: Which is prohibited in an IA's advertising?
questions.why: Guaranteed returns are prohibited.

questions.q: Which comes first in a plan?
questions.why: Protect first, then invest.
